Ben — thanks, this is actionable. I drafted a compact MAP and initial sizing notes below to unblock procurement. See attached MAP_Onramp_v0.3.xlsx and a quick sizing CSV. Key assumptions: 512 average tokens, 40 RPS bursts, 24/7 eval window for 4 weeks.

Summary (high level):
- Proposed trial capacity: 8 x A100-80GB equiv (initial), burst to 12 for peak days. Equivalent for Llama-3 70B: heavy KV cache usage suggests 10–12 GB per active session; for 13B models we recommend smaller nodes.
- Lead times: Hosted -> immediate; Dedicated pool (reserved) provisioning: 8–12 weeks typical procurement+hardware wait; Private VPC on customer cloud: 2–6 weeks depending on firewall/KMS approvals and infra team availability. On-prem air-gapped: up to 12+ weeks.
- MAP milestones (short):
  1) SOW draft & sign (Marissa) — target 12 business days from LOI
  2) Networking/KMS checklist complete (Atlas infra) — target 5 business days after SOW
  3) Provision Dedicated pool (Redwood ops) — 6–9 weeks after PO (conservative)
  4) Evaluation sprint (Atlas) — 3–4 weeks
  5) Post-eval tuning & quantization pass (Redwood/Atlas) — 1–2 weeks
  6) Final commitment/scale plan — within 10 business days after successful eval

Open asks for Atlas:
- Confirm preferred degree of dedicated isolation (fully dedicated GPUs vs shared hosts with tenant isolation).
- Preferred go-live window and any blackout dates for procurement.

I’ll run Rishi through the workload profile tomorrow and we’ll add a second tab with numeric compute-hours and cost estimates.

—Olga

Adding sizing detail after profiling the sample traces Ben shared. Quoted original below.

Short version (numbers):
- Llama-3 70B (float16/AMP): 1 live request uses ~28 GB of GPU memory at seq=512 with 4–8 concurrent KV caches depending on reuse. For sustained 40 RPS bursts we estimate needing 9 nodes (80GB-class) with batching and prefix caching to hit latency SLOs.
- 13B family (int8/quant): ~6 GB per request; can hit targets with 3–4 smaller nodes.
- Cost/commit trade: If Atlas chooses mixed pool (2x 70B nodes + 6x 13B nodes), you get 80% of eval coverage at ~55% of the committed spend vs all-70B pool.

Provisioning note: our Dedicated ordering pipeline requires a signed PO and region selection; we can reserve hardware capacity in our Q1 slot if PO arrives by Jan 7. That maps to an optimistic 6-week provisioning after PO. If you need Private VPC in GCP/Azure, we’ll need firewall IP ranges and KMS key ARN (2–6 week timeline depending on customer IT cadence).

I attached a small CSV with per-model simulated hours and a recommended initial pool config. I recommend the mixed pool above for the evaluation so you can iterate models without overspending.

- Rishi
Head of Inference Ops, Redwood Inference
